replication_status: exact (authors' code output 0.04429399 (0.0151523), N 15,243, equals printed Table 2 column (1) 0.044 (t 2.92; no SE printed), N 15,243, to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026; earlier label exact_package)
notes: Firm-year panel 1999-2009, 2,164 pseudonymized firms, 15,522 rows, 49 HQ states, unbalanced. utsa_dummy = 1 if the firm's CURRENT HQ state has enacted the UTSA by year t. sic2 (58 pseudonymized codes) is constant within firm in this file, so sic2-by-year FE enter via xt_vars. Firm-level treatment is not absorbing for movers: 107 firms change HQ state; 20 firms switch from 1 to 0 (105 rows), which run_spec.R drops (Hull fn 6), and about 25 firms switch on by moving into an already-treated state rather than by a law change. Genuine in-sample adoptions: Tennessee 2000 (29 firms) and Pennsylvania 2004 (67 firms). Firm-level cohorts in the runner: 2000-2006 and 2008 (mostly movers outside TN/PA). 574 never-treated firms (26.5%; states MA, NJ, NY, TX plus firms whose state adopts after 2009), 1,478 always-treated firms (68.3%; states adopting 1980-1998). Outcome SD in the authors' regression sample 0.38676, so authors' coef / SD = 0.114526. After dropping the 105 switch-off rows the same fixest regression gives 0.052752 (0.014128), N 15,417 (singletons kept); the runner's standardized TWFE should match that, not the published value.
